title: To the God of Instant Noodles
content:
I just whipped up a bowl of Buldak noodles,

When a friend sent over a photo—

A plate of crawfish we once shared.

What defines a "crawfish" now?

I’ve long lost the answer.

But then again,

What do Buldak noodles have to do with fire turkeys?

I suppose we’ll never know.

I’ve forgotten what summer even looks like.

Staring at the heavy snow outside, I can’t help but sigh.

If I were to leap,

Would it be the Past or the Present that kills me?

The Past has already happened, and the Present stands idly by.

By process of elimination, only the Future remains.

But the Future, armed with a perfect alibi,

Struts around with arrogant impunity.

So, what kills me

Is the absence of a future.

But oh, merciful God of Instant Noodles,

I once swore to You—

I would remain forever loyal to Shin Ramyun,

Never reaching my greedy hands toward the Buldak cult.

Yet here I am, standing in utter solitude,

Personally slaughtering my own vow.

Just as I once told my mother

I would never smoke.

Now I realize

That "forever" arrives much sooner than expected.

But oh, kind God of Instant Noodles,

Do You still remember?

We once fought side by side,

Despising the disciples of Buldak,

Deeming that filthy cuisine the darkest of heresies.

But I—but I—

At some untraceable moment,

Stopped feeling Your presence.

I curled up in a field of black rye,

Letting it swallow me whole.

That was the first time I cried with such stillness.

Are You still there, my Lord?

I choose to believe

That the snow outside

Is the penance You have cast down.

I kneel in Your boundless white, sobbing, confessing.

But oh, heartless God of Instant Noodles,

I cannot decipher Your oracles.

I don't understand why You left,

Abandoning me to this bitter winter,

Letting the frost pierce through my ribs.

In my moment of deepest despair,

It was the Buldak noodles

That took me into their embrace.

Buldak noodles are tasty,

But I don't like Buldak noodles.

You know this.

But I had no choice.

Between eternal darkness and total depravity,

I simply chose to survive.

But if—just if—

You ever descend upon this wasteland again,

Remember that field of black rye I told You about.

Erect a headstone for me.

Offer a pack of Shin Ramyun,

And perhaps a Matcha Latte,

To mourn me, and Your former glory.
excerpt: I must have been hallucinating at the time; I should have gone to bed earlier.
